pyramid.label: STATED (counted with `cargo test -- --list`, grouped by test file)
pyramid.versusPlan: DERIVED: test-plan.md section 3 planned about 40/20/30/10 percent. Actual is 33/48/15/4, so INT is heavier and PARITY and COMPAT lighter than planned in share terms. Nothing was added at a layer higher than planned (I-12): COMPAT tests exist only for BR-006, BR-007, BR-014 as planned, and the 44 PARITY tests cover 13 of 14 rules as planned. Share differences come from the many scenario-driven INT tests (int_service 42, int_routes 22) and from parity tests that loop over many cases inside one test function (a test count understates PARITY comparisons: wave-6 reports 576 parity comparisons). Not a defect.

runtime.oracleRequirement: The 56 tests in parity_* and compat_* need the Python oracle: uv, a pinned copy of the reference repo (/tmp/minidon-oracle-<sha>, uv sync --frozen) and Python 3.12. Without uv they cannot run. The other 236 do not need it.
runtime.budget: No numeric budget was found in the plan (OP-02: performance not tested, a gross-slowness check is the suite finishing in normal time). DERIVED: 50 s for the full suite and 3 s for the no-oracle part is well within a normal CI time for a suite of this size. Coverage instrumented run took about 80 s.

limits: Branch coverage not available on stable Rust, region coverage given instead.
main.rs coverage understates what the real-binary tests do (killed child process does not flush its profile).
Coverage on 18 files is of line execution, not of rule conformance. Mutation checks in build/wave-6.md are the evidence for assertion strength.
No reference to the Python repo was written (I-29); no file in minidon-rust was changed by this measurement.
